items.title: AI platform and database map protein phase separation across species
items.excerpt: NTU Singapore researchers used large language models to mine PubMed for phase-behavior data and built PLATO, a database of ~5,118 tested protein sequences, plus PhaseHub, which uses the MolPhase machine-learning predictor to map protein phase separation across 1,106 species (Molecular Plant).

items.title: How nature lovers can aid ecology with an assist from AI
items.excerpt: University of Michigan researchers used ChatGPT and Claude to find and classify species-interaction observations buried in eBird and iNaturalist comments, surfacing signs of nonnative plant spread on the U.S. West Coast; a task taking a student eight hours took Claude six minutes (PNAS).

items.title: AI reveals how coating thickness changes the link between surface roughness and pitting resistance
items.excerpt: Shibaura Institute of Technology researchers applied interpretable machine learning (random forest with SHAP and ALE analyses) to 90 steam-coated aluminum specimens and found the effect of surface roughness on pitting corrosion reverses near a 2,200 nm film thickness (npj Materials Degradation).

items.title: Just 10 minutes of AI use may erode persistence on hard tasks
items.excerpt: Three randomized trials with 1,222 participants found that about 10 minutes of AI assistance raised initial accuracy on math and reading problems, but once the tool was removed, users became less accurate and less persistent than people who never had it (Berkeley/CMU/MIT/Oxford/UCLA, COLM).

items.title: A new approach to sustainable AI: Offloading part of the computational burden onto light
items.excerpt: Koç University researchers built two photonic systems that move part of AI computation onto light: a programmable optical neural network that learns from experimental measurements (raising skin-lesion classification accuracy from 68% to 98%) and a multimode fiber laser that processes images at 85-99% accuracy with fewer trainable parameters (Communications Engineering / Communications Physics).

items.title: A unique shape, a 3D einstein tile, has been discovered
items.excerpt: AI helped uncover a special object that can fill space without repeating patterns

items.title: How attachment theory can help us understand AI relationships
items.excerpt: Attachment is the term psychologists use for the most significant relationships that hold people’s lives together

items.title: Is 'Attention' the Essence of Intelligence?
items.excerpt: A mathematical mechanism enables AI models to process language at scale, undergirding the current AI revolution. Our columnist asks: Why is attention the key?

items.title: 'Autonomy always begins with something a human hands it': Who's responsible when an AI agent goes rogue?
items.excerpt: Hacking incidents by AI agents are creating a legal minefield. The developers and deployers of rogue bots could be held liable.

items.title: OpenAI claims we've entered the AGI era — has GPT-6 Astra really demonstrated general intelligence?
items.excerpt: OpenAI says its newly launched GPT-6 Astra model brings humanity to the threshold of AGI, but external evaluators argue that inflated lab metrics and opaque testing obscure its true reliability.

items.title: When Imagining the Future of AI, Gen-Zers Are Not Optimistic
items.excerpt: A soon-to-be-published study shows Gen-Zers imagine more worrying than exciting events regarding AI, yet attitudes toward technology and one's politics play a role.

items.title: The "Good Enough" AI
items.excerpt: Winnicott’s ‘good enough’ parent theory offers a way to consider whether certain frictions in our AI interactions might help us grow.

items.title: The Impact of AI on Who We Are and Who We Become
items.excerpt: AI systems map preferences, patterns, and choices and influence them, too, creating an algorithmic self. We need to use AI consciously to manage threats to the human self.

items.title: We're putting too much faith in AI's ability to say no
items.excerpt: Today’s LLMs are engineered to disobey dangerous requests. But AI refusal is far from foolproof—and could become an instrument of repression.

items.title: Energy Department Announces New Genesis Mission Awards to Accelerate Scientific Capability
items.excerpt: The Department of Energy announced $159 million for 12 new Phase II Genesis Mission projects using AI and advanced computing.

items.title: The fall of Roe dramatically changed abortion access. This researcher used Reddit to capture how
items.excerpt: With research on abortion access barriers, STAT Wunderkind Betsy Pleasants is defining a framework for using AI tools without losing sight of the people behind the data.

items.title: Ai2 at COLM 2026: Open research, from models to agents for science
items.excerpt: Ai2 joined COLM 2026 to share advances in open language models, training infrastructure, and AI for science, including Olmo Hybrid, the Asta scientific-research agent ecosystem, and Bolmo byte-level models.
